full_source_record.title: Relate convergence performance to feasible samples, tolerance and physical time
full_source_record.task: Explain the response speed of power control and what it supports about deployment.
chain: Feasibility determines the sample population represented by conditional convergence statistics.
The reported experiment uses 10000 random trials, approximately 48 percent feasible cases and a tolerance within 1 percent of a 12 dB target; these are source-experiment settings.
The source separately reports infeasibility detection and discusses different implications of 0.01-second and 0.1-second iterations.
Theoretical convergence is conditional on feasibility and an appropriate step size; a small iteration count does not itself establish physical real-time performance.
full_source_record.diagnostic_relation: Check the statistical denominator, feasibility filtering, convergence threshold and available time budget before inferring overall success or deployment speed.
full_source_record.boundary: The source's feasible fraction and tolerance are not general standards. Static-propagation results do not automatically cover mobile or fast-fading tracking. Unknown iteration duration leaves a deployment claim unsupported rather than supplying an invented runtime.

full_source_record.title: Organize a long proof around traceable intermediate propositions and close its final claim
full_source_record.task: Explain how Costa-strategy achievable sum rate reaches broadcast-channel sum capacity, rather than merely proving an achievable scheme works.
full_source_record.premises: The vector Gaussian broadcast channel, total-power condition and source receiver structure require an achievable lower side and an upper bound valid for arbitrary strategies to meet.
chain: Relate the Costa achievable region to the reverse multiple-access channel's capacity region to establish the achievable side.
Use a receiver-cooperating point-to-point channel as a Sato upper bound and distinguish marginal from joint noise distributions when optimizing that bound.
Apply reciprocity to obtain an uplink cooperating channel with a quadratic cost.
Choose the cost matrix so that the cooperating uplink capacity meets the multiple-access sum capacity, closing the upper-bound and achievability argument.
A diagram links four channel types with different logical relations, while the conclusion recalls the steps rather than only repeating the capacity claim.
full_source_record.diagnostic_relation: Several correct lemmas do not establish a final capacity claim unless their dependencies and closing implication are supplied.
full_source_record.boundary: Achievability, upper bounds, reciprocity and equality of optimized values have different logical meanings; do not turn all links into unconditional equalities. Logical closure is required for the claim, but a diagram or a three-step presentation is optional.
full_source_record.verification_limit: The original analysis examined selected organization and diagram pages, without independently reproving every derivation in the preceding sections.
full_source_record.source_description: The stored pages link an achievable rate, a receiver-cooperation upper bound, reciprocity, and a witness that closes the capacity argument. A figure and staged proof outline communicate this chain.
full_source_record.analyst_assessment: The original companion already distinguishes necessary logical closure from optional diagrams and labels diagnostic transfer as unvalidated. Replace the sufficient-alternative label with nonexclusive expression options and retain the actual proof obligations.

Construct a design insensitive to the specified statistical variations under those conditions.

L03.selection_boundary: Load together only if a target extrapolates one metric or asymptotic order to broader performance equivalence.

full_source_record.title: Separate equivalence metrics to explain different performance despite identical asymptotic order
full_source_record.task: Clarify the high-SNR relationship between ZF and MMSE without treating one limiting similarity as equality of every performance metric.
full_source_record.premises: The source MIMO model and receive-antenna conditions distinguish output SNR, error rate, outage and diversity-multiplexing tradeoff.
chain: Identify the inference from ZF being the high-SNR limit of MMSE to equality of output SNR, error or outage performance.
Decompose MMSE output SNR into the ZF term and an additional term, retaining its statistical properties and high-SNR limit.
Distinguish a nonvanishing SNR gain from an asymptotic outage-capacity relationship.
Explain how both receivers can share a diversity-multiplexing tradeoff that does not capture the SNR gain.
State which comparisons coincide and which differ using the same results, rather than declaring broad equivalence or nonequivalence.
full_source_record.diagnostic_relation: Similarity of a limiting matrix or asymptotic slope answers only its specified comparison; it does not establish broader absence of performance differences.
full_source_record.boundary: Keep dimensions, coding conditions, metric definitions and limits. Source-model conclusions cannot extend to arbitrary receivers or channels.

full_source_record.source_description: The stored pages decompose the model-specific SNR relationship and distinguish a shared asymptotic diversity-multiplexing order from finite-SNR or outage differences.
full_source_record.analyst_assessment: The original companion already labels transfer as unvalidated and says other metrics are unnecessary without a broader equivalence claim. Its alternative options should be conditional on the target metric and model, rather than labeled sufficient.
